title: What Is Redis?
summary: What Redis is — an in-memory key-value store used as a cache, database, and message broker — plus the single-threaded model, how it compares to Memcached and a relational database, the Redis/Valkey ecosystem, and an honest licensing history.

title: Getting Started with redis-cli
summary: Install Redis (including with Docker), connect with redis-cli, and learn the essential session commands — PING, INFO, SELECT and the 16 logical databases, DBSIZE, CONFIG — plus a first look at the RESP request/response protocol.

title: Keys and Strings
summary: The Redis keyspace and key-naming conventions, the essential key commands, why KEYS is dangerous and SCAN is safe, and the String type in depth — SET options, atomic counters with INCR, and multi-key operations.

title: Lists
summary: The Redis List type: an ordered sequence you push and pop from either end in O(1). Build queues, stacks, and capped 'latest-N' lists, and use blocking pops (BLPOP) for producer/consumer patterns.

title: Hashes
summary: The Redis Hash type: a map of field-value pairs under one key, ideal for modeling objects. Learn HSET/HGET/HGETALL/HINCRBY, when a hash beats many string keys, and its memory advantages.

title: Sets
summary: The Redis Set type: an unordered collection of unique members. Learn SADD/SISMEMBER/SMEMBERS, the set-algebra commands (SINTER, SUNION, SDIFF), and patterns like tags, unique visitors, and relationships.

title: Sorted Sets
summary: The Redis Sorted Set: unique members each ranked by a numeric score. Learn ZADD/ZRANGE/ZRANK/ZINCRBY and build leaderboards, time-ordered feeds, and priority queues with O(log N) operations.

title: Expiration and Key Lifetime
summary: How Redis keys live and die: setting TTLs with EXPIRE/TTL/PERSIST, how passive and active expiration actually work, how writes affect a TTL, and a first look at maxmemory and eviction.

title: Bitmaps and HyperLogLog
summary: Two space-efficient tools built on strings: Bitmaps (per-bit flags via SETBIT/BITCOUNT/BITOP) for dense boolean tracking, and HyperLogLog (PFADD/PFCOUNT) for counting unique items at scale with tiny, fixed memory.

title: Publish/Subscribe
summary: Redis Pub/Sub messaging: publishers send to channels, subscribers receive in real time. Learn SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/PSUBSCRIBE, the fire-and-forget (at-most-once) delivery model, and when to choose Streams instead.

title: Streams
summary: The Redis Stream: a persistent, append-only log of entries you can replay by ID. Learn XADD/XREAD/XRANGE, consumer groups (XREADGROUP/XACK) for at-least-once processing, and how Streams compare to Pub/Sub and Lists.

title: Transactions
summary: Redis transactions with MULTI/EXEC/DISCARD: how commands are queued and run without interleaving, why there is NO rollback on errors, and how WATCH provides optimistic locking (check-and-set).

title: Lua Scripting and Functions
summary: Run custom logic atomically inside Redis with Lua: EVAL/EVALSHA, KEYS and ARGV, and why scripts are atomic. Plus Redis Functions (FUNCTION LOAD/FCALL) — the modern, persisted way to ship server-side logic.

title: Persistence: RDB and AOF
summary: How Redis survives restarts: RDB point-in-time snapshots versus the AOF append-only command log, the appendfsync durability trade-offs, using both together, and what 'in-memory' really means for your data.

title: Memory and Eviction
summary: Bounding Redis memory with maxmemory and the eight eviction policies (noeviction, allkeys-*, volatile-*). Why LRU and LFU are approximated by sampling, and how to pick a policy for a cache versus mixed data.

title: Caching Patterns
summary: The patterns that make Redis a great cache: cache-aside, read-through, write-through, and write-behind; TTL strategies; the cache-stampede problem and its fixes; invalidation; and server-assisted client-side caching.

title: Pipelining and Performance
summary: Make Redis fast: pipelining to eliminate round-trip latency, the single-threaded core plus optional I/O threads, diagnosing slow commands with SLOWLOG and LATENCY, benchmarking, and avoiding O(N) command traps.

title: Replication
summary: Redis replication: a primary streams changes to read-only replicas with REPLICAOF. Learn full vs partial resync, why replication is asynchronous (and what that means for consistency and failover), and how to scale reads.

title: High Availability with Sentinel
summary: Redis Sentinel adds automatic failover to a primary/replica setup: it monitors instances, agrees on failure via a quorum, promotes a replica, and tells clients the new primary. How it differs from Cluster.

title: Redis Cluster
summary: Redis Cluster shards data across 16384 hash slots on multiple primaries, each with replicas. Learn how keys map to slots (CRC16), MOVED/ASK redirects, hash tags for multi-key ops, and Cluster's consistency limits.

title: Security
summary: Locking down Redis: why it must never face the internet, authentication with requirepass and ACL users, encrypting traffic with TLS, protected mode, and disabling or renaming dangerous commands.

title: Observability and Operations
summary: Running Redis day to day: reading INFO metrics (hit rate, memory, evictions), using MONITOR/SLOWLOG/LATENCY safely, keyspace notifications, CLIENT commands, backups and rolling upgrades, and the common production pitfalls.

title: The Redis 8 Data and Query Engine
summary: Beyond the core types: JSON documents, the Query Engine (secondary indexing and search), probabilistic structures, time series, and Vector Sets for similarity search — all now part of Redis Open Source 8 (formerly Redis Stack).

title: Data Modeling and Capstone
summary: Bringing it together: choosing the right data structure, designing keys, avoiding anti-patterns, and combining structures into real features — a rate limiter, session store, leaderboard, and job queue — plus when NOT to use Redis.
